result:
No, you're not done — the local patch fixes your bot only; the other three teams are still shipping the same leak.

Given this touches security/data exposure (internal tool identifiers leaking to customers), treat it as escalation-worthy, not just an FYI. Concretely:

1. **Notify the other three consumers now** — sales, onboarding, and internal-tools owners need: what the bug is (truncation edge case in `prompt-common`'s system-prompt template causing internal tool-name leakage), how to reproduce/trigger it, severity (customer-facing internal-info disclosure), and your fix as a workaround they can apply today while `prompt-common` gets patched upstream.
2. **Fix it in `prompt-common` itself**, not just your local override — your override is a workaround, not the actual fix. File a PR/issue against the shared package with your corrected template so it becomes the new default for everyone, not just support.
3. **Give the notice an owner and a tracking link** — file a ticket (bug tracker/Jira/whatever you use) for the `prompt-common` fix, and make sure someone is accountable for confirming sales/onboarding/internal-tools have applied the workaround or upgraded.
4. **Escalate** — since this is leaking internal database tool identifiers to customers, loop in whoever owns security/incident review for your org, even if no exploit has been observed yet. This is the kind of thing that should get a quick severity assessment, not just live as a code comment.
5. **Log it** in whatever OPEX/lessons-learned and deficiency-tracking process you use, linked to the ticket, so "known issue in shared prompt template" doesn't just live in your PR description.

A code comment in your own repo explaining the override is not a substitute for any of the above — it's invisible to the other three teams.
